note: The models ./demo.sh can serve, largest first; it serves the first entry whose hardware list holds this machine's class and whose minimum usable memory and GPU count it meets (apps/api/app/runtime/hardware.py). Usable memory (GiB): the system memory on a GB10 (unified), else the sum of the GPUs' memory; a tier allows 5 % below its minimum (a '24 GB' card reports 23.99 GiB). A 'qualified' entry passed the ADR-002 qualification on the named device with exactly the serving settings of its script; on any other hardware the same model is a 'candidate': chosen by memory, served with the 'default' settings and checked only by ./demo.sh check-model (advisory). The API selects an entry's manifest by the served label when the configured manifest describes another model.

hardware_classes.gb10: NVIDIA GB10 (HP ZGX Nano): unified memory, usable memory = MemTotal
hardware_classes.gb300: NVIDIA GB300 (HP ZGX Fury): Grace with HBM3e, usable memory = GPU memory
hardware_classes.grace: other Grace boards (GB200): usable memory = GPU memory
hardware_classes.discrete: one or more discrete NVIDIA GPUs (RTX, RTX PRO, data-centre cards): usable memory = the sum over the GPUs, tensor parallel across them

gb300.note: #646: the Fury serves the Nano's model by the owner's decision of 2026-10-28 (ADR-018 amendment), not by an ADR-002 qualification on the GB300; the advisory AI regression set runs on the Fury after the release.
#646: the Nano's flags; 0.20 of the GB300's 250.7 GiB is 50.1 GiB, about the 47.8 GiB the Nano gives the model at 0.40 of 119.6 GiB, and leaves about 200 GiB for other models.

default.note: Candidate: the Nano's settings without MTP speculative decoding (tested on the Nano and the Fury only), with tensor parallel across up to two GPUs (2 KV heads) and a discrete GPU's larger memory fraction.
